title: Contingency accordion rollout chef and ops notes - Mar 2029 (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational-first draft for a staggered rollout pattern ("accordion") with explicit contingency lanes and a nightwatch playlist. Goal: make the 72h window after release predictable and scriptable for small teams running cross-region model or infra changes.

Quick summary (one-liner):
- Stagger traffic across regions in a compressible accordion pattern, observe telemetry gates, and have per-lane rollback and throttling cookbooks ready.

High-level flow (ordered):
1) Preflight checks (T-72h to T-2h): config freeze, smoke tasks, quota checks, telemetry baseline snapshot.
2) Canary lane (T0): 1% global traffic or single-region 10% for region-limited features. 4x smoke cycles, 30m steady-state checks.
3) Accordion expansion (T+1h to T+24h): double traffic lane-by-lane with 30–60m hold times and automated metric gates.
4) Nightwatch (T+0 to T+72h): 4x daily sampling windows, on-call handoffs, scripted remediation.
5) Aftercare (T+72h+): retrospective, artifacts, and archived release notes.

Preflight checklist (owner in parens) - must be green before any traffic shift:
- Feature flags toggled to canary state (Feature Flags) (James Park)
- Canary image pinned in deployment manifest (Infra) (Li Wei)
- Smoke suite pass on staging and a mirrored prod-slice (QA) (Aria Gomez)
- Token/billing/quotas sanity check for Dedicated pools (Finance/Infra) (Marta)
- Runtime config: kv-cache warming pre-seed, batch-size cap, quant profile set (Serving Runtime) (Li Wei)
- Telemetry baseline snapshot captured (observability) (James)
- Customer-impact list exported and communicated to CS (Customer Success) (Aria)

Canary lane runbook (T0, owner: James Park) - actionable steps:
- Deploy canary and hold at 0% ingress until deployment passes probe (0–5m)
- Shift 1% traffic globally or route 10% within single region for 10m
- Run canary smoke checklist: token-level latency p50/p95, error-rate, model-quality quick helloworld prompts, and tail-latency peek
- If any gate trips -> immediate rollback to previous stable image and trigger incident channel #release-ops
- If gated green after 30m -> mark lane healthy and record snapshot IDs (telemetry)
